title: European Commission proposes revised Frontex mandate and digital return procedures
excerpt: The proposal seeks to enhance border management and modernize return, readmission and reintegration procedures across the European Union.
bodyHtml:
The European Commission announced on October 27, 2026, a proposal to revise the mandate of Frontex and to digitalise return, readmission and reintegration procedures. The initiative seeks to provide the agency with increased operational capacity, improved planning, and better access to equipment and surveillance tools to manage external borders.

Under the proposed rules, the European Commission said Frontex would gain the authority to monitor social media content for developments relevant to border management and act against content it identifies as illegal. The agency would also become the central actor for return-related support, including strategic planning and reintegration. The proposal includes the creation of a digital backbone to connect authorities and facilitate secure information exchange regarding travel documents and return operations.

The European Commission stated that the new regulations are intended to simplify procedures and reduce administrative burdens for Member States. The proposal follows the entry into force of the new Return Regulation on 16 October 2026.
topic: Remarks by Executive Vice-President Virkkunen and Commissioner Brunner on strengthening Frontex and the digitalisation of the return process
